ios.desc:
A calorie counter only works if you are still opening it next week. People leave because writing the meal down takes longer than eating it.

Limotein is the food diary you can finish. Say what you ate, snap the plate, scan the package, search, or type it the way you would text someone. Coach drafts the calories and macros, protein included. You confirm once. Nothing is saved until you do, and then you get on with the day.

Intermittent fasting usually means a second app. The timer sits in one place and the food log in another, so you lose the clock as soon as you go to eat. Here they stay together. Choose a 16/8, a lighter window, or one meal a day, or set your own hours. You see time elapsed or time left on Today, on your home screen, and on Apple Watch. Basic fasting stays free forever. Your window, the timer, and starting and ending the fast do not expire when a trial ends. When the window opens, that meal goes in the same diary.

You might have come here to count calories. You might have come for the fast. Either way it is one day. The fast says when eating starts. The diary says whether protein survived that window. You are not keeping two streaks in two apps and hoping they still describe the same Tuesday.

A plan that only survives a quiet week will not last. A dinner out, a trip, a late night, or a day you are ill can loosen the calorie range while protein stays in view. Log a travel day from whatever you actually ate. On a recovery day the deficit comes off: rest, hydrate, eat simply. Pause a day and it stays out of the score. The rest of the week does not move.

What you are trying to hold is usually one thing. Lose weight, and still eat enough protein. Maintain, and care about the food. Build muscle, with protein across the day. Eat for the training you did. Limotein sets calorie and macro targets from your body, your activity, and your pace. You can change them.

Coach already has today's log. You talk to it the way the day actually went, and nothing is saved until you confirm.

The plate is mixed and you will not weigh it. Photograph it. Coach names the foods, estimates each portion, totals the calories, and waits.
Lunch was small and dinner has to carry the protein. Ask how much protein is left, or ask what is left today and you get protein and calories together.
You logged half the meal and got pulled away. Hand that meal back. Coach continues from the foods already there, and does not add them a second time.

show_hn.title: Show HN: Limotein, AI-powered food tracker (voice, photo, or text input)

quotes.text:
Hi HN,

I built Limotein, a mobile app that simplifies food tracking using AI. The frustration of manually entering every ingredient, scanning barcodes, or building recipes from scratch pushed me to create something easier.

With Limotein, you can:

Speak, take a photo, or write what you ate

The app uses AI to estimate calories, protein, carbs, and fat

Tracks your meals across the day, and gives weekly/monthly stats

Works for takeout, homemade food, and even vague meal descriptions

My stack: Flutter (cross-platform), Firebase, OpenAI for natural language parsing and image analysis, RevenueCat for subscription, and Mixpanel for analytics.

iOS:

Download: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6740625021

Redeem offer: https://apps.apple.com/redeem?ctx=offercodes&id=6740625021&code=REDDIT100

Android:

Download: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.limbool.limotein

Redeem on Android in the app during subscription using REDDIT100 code
